rv.q: It’s a wickedly entertaining show that balances proper spectacle with heartfelt drama.
It's not easy being green, but that doesn't stop Wicked from being a solid West End favourite.

No one could accuse Wicked of being a great musical - indeed at times it's a bit of a mess - but it proves far more enjoyable than I had dared to hope, and deserves a wider audience than adolescent schoolgirls.
In terms of musical spectacle, 'The Lion King' is its only London rival.

But, although it has been a hit in New York, it seems all too typical of the modern Broadway musical: efficient, knowing and highly professional but more like a piece of industrial product than something that genuinely touches the heart or mind.
More than 15 years after Wicked flew into the West End, the Olivier Award-winning musical is still an evening of sheer musical theatre bliss.
Stephen Schwartz's score, arguably his best so far, is an ebullient mix of grandiose anthems and lyrical ballads.
The production manages to feel at once overblown and empty.
If you haven't seen it already, put this show to the top of your list!
In the meantime, see these themes being celebrated in this stunning production.
I give this production 5 stars, why didn't I see it sooner!

The whole cast sing and dance their hearts out in what is a very satisfying evening of theatre that might just miss out on the ultimate accolades for the lack of a couple of production numbers that would ensure massive sales of the soundtrack CD.
